basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering / Sanitary Appliances and Water Fittings (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Sanitary Appliances and Water Fittings Sectional Committee, CED 3, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements for materials, dimensions, testing methods (including hydraulic pressure, crushing strength, water absorption, acid resistance, and magnesium sulphate soundness), and sampling scales for chemically resistant glazed stoneware pipes and fittings used for conveying highly corrosive industrial effluents and aggressive chemical sewage.

allied_standards.relevance: Unifies risk mitigation, mandating regular integrity checks and maintenance of hazardous chemical sewage lines to prevent structural escapes.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Civil Engineering Department / Sanitaryware and Pipes)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) directly on the ceramic bodies of pipes and fittings. Conformance with IS 3006 is legally mandatory under State Public Works Department (PWD) specifications, municipal water-supply and sewerage corporation bylaws, and industrial chemical factory piping supply tenders across India.

requirements.detail: The interior of pipes and fittings must carry a ceramic glaze applied prior to firing, which melts and fuses with the body to form an impervious, chemically inert glass-like protective seal.
Straight pipes must withstand an internal hydraulic test pressure of 0.3 MPa on the barrels, and fittings must withstand 0.15 MPa, without showing any signs of injury or leakage.
The hydraulic pressure must be applied at a rate not exceeding 0.075 MPa in 5 seconds, and full pressure must be maintained for at least 5 seconds after extracting all air.

The mean thickness of barrels and sockets is determined separately by making several measurements, adding the measured least thickness (excluding the groove) to the greatest thickness, and dividing by two.

The interior of sockets and the exterior of spigots must be grooved circumferentially. Grooving on the spigot must extend over a length equal to 1.5 times the depth of the socket, with a groove depth between 1 mm and 2 mm.

Specimens must be submerged in a saturated boiling magnesium sulphate solution (specific gravity 1.295 to 1.308) for 2 hours, and then dried to a constant mass in an oven at not less than 110°C, repeating the process for at least five cycles.

The crushing test rig requires wood facings lined with rubber bearing strips on the top and bottom beams. The bottom facing is centered on the beam flange by hardwood strips, allowing Shape A or Shape B cross-sections.

The vertical crushing load is applied to the top bearing at a point equal to one-half of the overall length (including socket). The bearing must be free to rotate vertically through the longitudinal center line.

The water absorption test evaluates whether the clay body is fully vitrified. The lot conforms to standard limits if the calculated statistical threshold (mean + 0.6 times range) does not exceed the specified maximum limit.
For acid resistance, magnesium sulphate soundness, and crushing strength tests, all individual test specimens selected in the statistical sample must successfully satisfy the requirements.

Observed or calculated dimensions, test pressures, and weight differences must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 3006 : 1979 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification establishing technical, dimensional, material, and performance requirements for chemically resistant glazed stoneware pipes and fittings used for conveying aggressive chemical and industrial effluents. Developed under Sectional Committee CED 3 and reaffirmed in 2022, the standard regulates straight pipes and fittings—such as bends, junctions, channels, and gully traps—to ensure complete chemical inertness and structural reliability. It mandates a prior-to-firing ceramic glaze, details high-integrity pressure testing (withstanding 0.3 MPa on pipes and 0.15 MPa on fittings), establishes mechanical load crushing test setups, defines soundness evaluations using five boiling cycles in saturated magnesium sulphate, and enforces strict statistical sampling controls under Appendix E to verify water-absorption, acid-resistance, and physical durability thresholds.
